readings.title: The Death of Eli
readings.subtitle: The Esteem Has Departed
readings.text: [1 Samuel 4:12] And a man of Binyamin ran from the battle line the same day, and came to Shiloh with his garments torn and dirt on his head. [13] And he came in and saw Ěli, sitting on a seat by the wayside watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And the man came into the city and reported it, and all the city cried out. [14] And Ěli heard the noise of the outcry and said, “What is the noise of this uproar?” And the man came hastily and informed Ěli. [15] Now Ěli was ninety-eight years old and his eyes were so dim that he was unable to see. [16] And the man said to Ěli, “I am he who came from the battle. And I fled today from the battle line.” And he said, “What was the matter, my son?” [17] And the messenger answered and said, “Yisra’ěl has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. And your two sons have died, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, and the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> has been captured.” [18] And it came to be, when he made mention of <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, that Ěli fell off the seat backward by the side of the gate. And his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he ruled Yisra’ěl forty years. [19] And his daughter-in-law, Pineḥas’ wife, was pregnant, about to bear. And when she heard the news that the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was captured, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth, because her pains came upon her. [20] And about the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Do not fear, for you have borne a son.” But she did not answer, nor did she set her heart to it. [21] And she called the child Iḵaḇoḏ, saying, “The esteem has departed from Yisra’ěl!” because the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was taken and because of her father-in-law and her husband. [22] And she said, “The esteem has departed from Yisra’ěl, for the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was taken.”

readings.title: The Ark in the House of Dagon
readings.subtitle: The Hand of YeHoVaH Against the Philistines
readings.text: [1 Samuel 5:1] And the Philistines took <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> and brought it from Eḇen Ha‛ězer to Ashdoḏ, [2] and the Philistines took <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> and brought it into the house of Daḡon and set it by Daḡon. [3] And the Ashdoḏites rose early in the morning and saw Daḡon fallen on its face to the ground before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. So they took <dn>את</dn> Daḡon and put it in its place again. [4] And they arose early the next morning and saw Daḡon fallen on its face to the ground before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the head of Daḡon and both the palms of its hands cut off, on the threshold, only Daḡon itself was left of it. [5] That is why, to this day, the priests of Daḡon and all who come into Daḡon’s house do not tread on the threshold of Daḡon in Ashdoḏ. [6] But the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was heavy on the Ashdoḏites, and <dn>He</dn> wasted them and struck <dn>את</dn> them with tumours – Ashdoḏ and its borders. [7] And when the men of Ashdoḏ saw this, they said, “Let not the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl remain with us, for <dn>His</dn> hand has been hard on us, and on Daḡon our mighty one.” [8] Then they sent and gathered to them all the princes of the Philistines, and said, “What do we do with the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl?” And they answered, “Let the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl be removed to Gath.” And they removed <dn>את</dn> the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl. [9] And it came to be, after they removed it, that the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was against the city with a very great destruction. And <dn>He</dn> struck <dn>את</dn> the men of the city, from the least to the greatest, and tumours broke out on them. [10] They then sent <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> to Eqron. And it came to be, as the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Eqron, that the Eqronites cried out, saying, “They have removed the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl to us, to kill us and our people!” [11] And they sent and gathered together all the princes of the Philistines, and said, “Send away <dn>את</dn> the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, and let it return to its own place, so that it does not kill us and our people.” For there had come a deadly destruction throughout all the city – the hand of <dn>Elohim</dn> was very heavy there. [12] And the men who did not die were stricken with tumours, and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.

readings.title: The Guilt Offering
readings.subtitle: The Cows Go to Beth Shemesh
readings.text: [1 Samuel 6:1] And the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was in the field of the Philistines for seven new moons. [2] And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, “What do we do with the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? Let us know with what we should send it to its place.” [3] And they said, “If you send away <dn>את</dn> the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, do not send it empty, but you shall certainly return it to <dn>Him</dn> with a guilt offering. Then you are going to be healed, and it shall be known to you why <dn>His</dn> hand does not turn aside from you.” [4] And they said, “What is the guilt offering which we return to <dn>Him</dn>?” And they answered, “The number of the princes of the Philistines: five golden tumours and five golden rats. For the same plague was on all of you and on your princes. [5] “And you shall make images of your tumours and images of your rats that ruin the land, and you shall give esteem to the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl. It could be that <dn>He</dn> does lift <dn>His</dn> hand from you, from your mighty ones, and from your land. [6] “And why do you harden your hearts as the Mitsrites and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When <dn>He</dn> had severely dealt with them, did they not send them away, and they went? [7] “And now, take and make a new wagon, and two milk cows which have never been yoked, and hitch <dn>את</dn> the cows to the wagon. And take their calves home, away from them. [8] “And take <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and put it on the wagon. And put <dn>את</dn> the objects of gold which you are returning to <dn>Him</dn> as a guilt offering in a chest by its side, and send it away, and it shall go. [9] “And you shall see, if it goes up the way to its own border, to Běyth Shemesh, then <dn>He</dn> has done us <dn>את</dn> this great evil. But if not, then we shall know that <dn>His</dn> hand has not come against us – an accident it was to us.” [10] And the men did so and took two milk cows and hitched them to the wagon, and shut up <dn>את</dn> their calves at home. [11] And they put <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the wagon, and <dn>את</dn> the chest with the gold rats and the images of their tumours. [12] And the cows went straight for the way to Běyth Shemesh, and went along the highway, bellowing as they went, and did not turn aside, right or left. And the princes of the Philistines went after them to the border of Běyth Shemesh. [13] And they of Běyth Shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley. And they lifted their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it. [14] And the wagon came into the field of Yehoshua of Běyth Shemesh and stood there, and there was a great stone. So they split the wood of the wagon and offered the cows as an ascending offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] And the Lěvites took down <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the chest that was with it, in which were the objects of gold, and put them on the great stone. And the men of Běyth Shemesh offered ascending offerings and slaughtered slaughterings the same day to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [16] And when the five princes of the Philistines saw it, they returned to Eqron the same day. [17] And these are the gold tumours which the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: one for Ashdoḏ, one for Azzah, one for Ashqelon, one for Gath, one for Eqron, [18] and the gold rats, by the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five princes, both walled cities and country villages, even as far as the great meadow on which they placed <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, remain to this day in the field of Yehoshua of Běyth Shemesh.

readings.title: The Ark at Beth Shemesh
readings.subtitle: Who Is Able to Stand Before YeHoVaH?
readings.text: [1 Samuel 6:19] And <dn>He</dn> struck among the men of Běyth Shemesh, for they had looked into the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dn>He</dn> struck among the people seventy men, and the people mourned because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> struck among the people, a great smiting. [20] And the men of Běyth Shemesh said, “Who is able to stand before this set-apart <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>? And to whom shall <dn>He</dn> go from us?” [21] And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Qiryath Ye‛arim, saying, “The Philistines have brought back <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Come down, take it up to you.” [1 Samuel 7:1] And the men of Qiryath Ye‛arim came and took <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and brought it into the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ on the hill, and set apart <dn>את</dn> El‛azar his son to guard <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] And it came to be, from the day that the ark remained in Qiryath Ye‛arim, that the time increased, it came to be twenty years.

readings.title: Thus Far YeHoVaH Has Helped Us
readings.subtitle: Samuel Judges Israel
readings.text: And all the house of Yisra’ěl lamented after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] And Shemu’ěl spoke to all the house of Yisra’ěl, saying, “If you return to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with all your hearts, then put away <dn>את</dn> the foreign mighty ones and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and serve <dn>Him</dn> only, so that <dn>He</dn> delivers you from the hand of the Philistines.” [4] And the children of Yisra’ěl put away <dn>את</dn> the Ba‛als and <dn>את</dn> Ashtaroth, and served <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> only. [5] And Shemu’ěl said, “Gather <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ěl to Mitspah and let me pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for you.” [6] And they gathered to Mitspah and drew water, and poured it out before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they fasted that day, and said there, “We have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” And Shemu’ěl rightly ruled the children of Yisra’ěl at Mitspah. [7] And when the Philistines heard that the children of Yisra’ěl had gathered together at Mitspah, the princes of the Philistines went up against Yisra’ěl. And the children of Yisra’ěl heard of it, and were afraid of the Philistines. [8] And the children of Yisra’ěl said to Shemu’ěl, “Do not cease to cry out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> for us, that <dn>He</dn> would save us from the hand of the Philistines.” [9] And Shemu’ěl took a suckling lamb and offered it as an ascending offering, completely, to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Shemu’ěl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for Yisra’ěl, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered him. [10] And it came to be, as Shemu’ěl offered up the ascending offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Yisra’ěl. But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> thundered with a great noise on that day on the Philistines, and troubled them, and they were smitten before Yisra’ěl. [11] And the men of Yisra’ěl went out from Mitspah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them as far as below Běyth Kar. [12] And Shemu’ěl took a stone and set it up between Mitspah and Shěn, and called its name Eḇen Ha‛ězer, saying, “Thus far <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has helped us.” [13] Thus the Philistines were humbled, and no longer came into the border of Yisra’ěl. And the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was against the Philistines all the days of Shemu’ěl. [14] And the cities which the Philistines had taken from Yisra’ěl were returned to Yisra’ěl, from Eqron to Gath. And Yisra’ěl recovered <dn>את</dn> its border from the hands of the Philistines. And there was peace between Yisra’ěl and the Amorites. [15] And Shemu’ěl rightly ruled Yisra’ěl all the days of his life, [16] and each year he made the rounds of Běyth Ěl, and Gilgal, and Mitspah, and rightly ruled Yisra’ěl in all those places. [17] Then he returned to Ramah, for his home was there. And there he rightly ruled Yisra’ěl, and there he built a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Give Us a Sovereign to Rule Us
readings.subtitle: They Have Rejected Me
readings.text: [1 Samuel 8:1] And it came to be, when Shemu’ěl was old, that he made <dn>את</dn> his sons rulers over Yisra’ěl. [2] And the name of his first-born was Yo’ěl, and the name of his second, Aḇiyah, rulers in Be’ěrsheḇa. [3] But his sons did not walk in his ways, and turned aside after own gain, and took bribes, and twisted right-ruling. [4] And all the elders of Yisra’ěl gathered together and came to Shemu’ěl at Ramah, [5] and said to him, “Look, you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint for us a sovereign to rule us like all the nations.” [6] But the word was evil in the eyes of Shemu’ěl when they said, “Give us a sovereign to rule us.” So Shemu’ěl prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ěl, <dq>“Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected <dn>Me</dn> from reigning over them.</dq> [8] <dq>According to all the works which they have done since the day that <dn>I</dn> brought them up out of Mitsrayim, even to this day – forsaking <dn>Me</dn> and serving other mighty ones – so they are doing to you too.</dq> [9] <dq>And now, listen to their voice, but you shall certainly warn them, and shall make known to them <dn>את</dn> the ruling of the sovereign who does reign over them.”</dq>

readings.title: The Ruling of the Sovereign
readings.subtitle: The People Refused to Listen
readings.text: [1 Samuel 8:10] And Shemu’ěl spoke <dn>את</dn> all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the people who asked him for a sovereign, [11] and said, “This is the ruling of the sovereign who does reign over you: <dn>He</dn> shall take <dn>את</dn> your sons and appoint them for <dn>his</dn> own chariots and to be <dn>his</dn> horsemen, and they shall run before <dn>his</dn> chariots, [12] and appoint commanders over <dn>his</dn> thousands and commanders over <dn>his</dn> fifties, or to plough <dn>his</dn> ground and reap <dn>his</dn> harvest, or to make <dn>his</dn> weapons, and equipment for <dn>his</dn> chariots. [13] “And <dn>את</dn> your daughters <dn>he</dn> is going to take to be perfumers, and cooks, and bakers. [14] “And <dn>את</dn> the best of your fields, and your vineyards, and your olive-trees <dn>he</dn> is going to take and give them to <dn>his</dn> servants. [15] “And a tenth of your grain and your vintage <dn>he</dn> is going to take and give it to <dn>his</dn> officers and servants. [16] “And <dn>את</dn> your male servants and <dn>את</dn> your female servants and <dn>את</dn> your best young men and <dn>את</dn> your donkeys <dn>he</dn> is going to take and use for <dn>his</dn> own work. [17] “A tenth of your sheep <dn>he</dn> is going to take, and you are to be <dn>his</dn> servants. [18] “And you shall cry out in that day because of your sovereign whom you have chosen for yourselves, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not going to answer you in that day.” [19] However, the people refused to listen to the voice of Shemu’ěl, and said, “No, but let a sovereign be over us. [20] Then we shall be, we also, like all the nations, and our sovereign shall rule us and go out before us and fight our battles.” [21] And Shemu’ěl heard <dn>את</dn> all the words of the people, and he repeated them in the hearing of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [22] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ěl, <dq>“Listen to their voice, and make them a sovereign.”</dq> And Shemu’ěl said to the men of Yisra’ěl, “Each of you go to his city.”
